To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the neurotoxicity of glutamate and the neuroprotection by GABA and serotonin are mediated by the same receptors and intracellular pathways.
neurotransmitters are involved in the control of neuronal cytoarchitecture and that these effects are mediated by intracellular signaling cascades.

neurotransmitters, besides their role in trans-synaptic communication, are also important in the control of neuronal morphology, and that this is achieved by modulation of intracellular signaling cascades.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the neurotransmitter dopamine in the development and maintenance of the nervous system.
the mechanisms by which neurotransmitters regulate neuronal morphology and survival.
the molecular and biochemical aspects of neuronal plasticity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
neurotransmitters can regulate neuronal morphology, survival, and function.
neurotransmitter receptors are involved in the regulation of neuronal outgrowths, plasticity and death.

, although neurotransmitter receptors are expressed in neurons throughout life and can be involved in the modulation of neuronal structure and function, the exact role of neurotransmitters and their receptors in the development and maintenance of the nervous system is far from clear and awaits further investigation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the neurotransmitter system is an important player in neuronal development, plasticity and death.
the nervous system is a dynamic, self-organized system that is constantly changing its structure in response to its environment.
the neurotransmitters and their receptors are not only the tools of communication but also the tools of neuronal plasticity and survival.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the neurotransmitter systems are not only involved in the communication between neurons, but also in the regulation of neuronal cytoarchitecture and function, and that this may be of great significance for normal development and function, as well as for pathological processes.
neurotransmitters, which have been thought to only mediate intercellular communication, can also regulate neuronal cytoarchitecture in a variety of ways.
neurotransmitters can be used as powerful tools to manipulate neuronal cytoarchitecture.
